Unpopular opinion: Most FX traders look at the wrong chart. 📊

They watch the spot rate. They should be watching the real exchange rate against purchasing power parity.

Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (Journal of Finance, 2013) showed FX value works as a unified factor alongside equities, bonds, and commodities. The mechanism is patience, not prediction.

Here's the complete logic:

🔹 PPP. Anchor every currency to its purchasing power parity benchmark using point-in-time CPI data (no look-ahead).
🔹 RANK currencies by negative 5-year real exchange rate change. Cheap currencies rise to the top.
🔹 LONG the cheap tercile, SHORT the expensive. Use forwards, rank-weighted.
🔹 HOLD. Half-life is 3-5 years. This is a slow factor.
🔹 PAIR with FX momentum. They're negatively correlated, so the combo diversifies.

Why it works: real exchange rates mean-revert because trade flows, capital movement, and inflation pressure pull them back. It just takes years.

Why retail can't capture it: the holding period kills them. They want monthly P&L, the factor wants multi-year patience.
